verdict.rationale: ClickUp's integration directory lists a first-party GitHub integration that syncs issues 'between GitHub and ClickUp', which implies two-way sync. The GitLab integration only says it links issues to tasks. Both claims are one-line directory blurbs with no detail on how the sync works. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of bi-directional field/status sync, conflict handling and sync scope, issue sync for Bitbucket, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineer, I can keep tasks bi-directionally synced with my code repository's issue tracker instead of duplicating data

citations.quote: Sync commits, branches, pull requests, and issues between GitHub and ClickUp to track development progress without switching tools.
Link GitLab commits, branches, pull requests, and issues with ClickUp Tasks for real-time visibility and streamlined development.
